themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Flatbush
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 21 THIS WEEK, a 500% jump from the 8-week baseline average of 3.5 complaints per week, signaling a potential coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating street maintenance in CD 309.
evidence: 21 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike)
Z-score of 6.19 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Spike is concentrated in current week, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods or corridors being targeted? Interview Parks/Sanitation about response protocols.
Is this connected to gang activity, art crews, or general disorder? Speak with precinct and local business owners on frontline.

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Three food poisoning complaints filed THIS WEEK represent a 700% spike from the 8-week average of 0.4 complaints per week, warranting investigation into a potential foodborne illness outbreak or contamination in local establishments.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase)
Z-score of 5.42 indicates anomaly well above normal variation
Cluster timing suggests possible single source or simultaneous incidents
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or food vendors are implicated? Cross-reference with DOHMH inspection records and outbreak notifications.
Have residents reported similar symptoms? Speak with complainants to identify common source or venue.

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints jumped to 39 LAST WEEK, a 380% increase from the 8-week baseline of 8.1 per week, indicating potential citywide or district-wide water main breaks, pressure issues, or pump failures affecting buildings in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 39 water system complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (380% spike)
Z-score of 5.75 indicates highly significant statistical anomaly
Combined with 464 water leak complaints and 597 plumbing complaints in 90-day volume, signals infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Are specific neighborhoods experiencing outages or low pressure? Map complaint locations and contact DEP for incident reports.
Is this tied to aging infrastructure, recent construction, or seasonal demand? Interview DEP and building managers on root cause.

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Ten asbestos complaints reported 2 WEEKS AGO represent a 1043% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.9 per week, suggesting multiple buildings undergoing renovation/demolition or discovery of hazardous materials in older Flatbush housing stock.
evidence: 10 asbestos complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1043% increase)
Z-score of 8.66 is the highest statistical anomaly in dataset
325 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (186 alterations) correlates with renovation-triggered asbestos discovery
reporting_angles: Which buildings are reporting asbestos? Cross-reference complaint addresses with DOB alteration permits and HPD records.
Are contractors properly notifying tenants and following EPA abatement protocols? Interview affected residents and inspect DOHMH compliance.

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Vehicle Dumping
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned vehicle complaints reached 15 LAST WEEK, a 253% increase from the 8-week average of 4.2 per week, indicating a potential uptick in vehicle abandonment or delayed NYPD towing in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 15 abandoned vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (253% spike)
Z-score of 4.24 indicates statistically significant deviation
Aligns with broader illegal parking complaints (2,047 in 90 days) and street clutter issues
reporting_angles: Are specific blocks or commercial corridors being used as dumping grounds? Map complaints and conduct street audit.
Is NYPD towing response time degraded? Interview 311 liaisons and request tow data from NYPD Traffic Division.
